business.body: CyberTech is an engineering-led technology services company built around three focus areas: enterprise cloud, geospatial, and SAP transformation. It delivers Esri ArcGIS-based geospatial services, SAP S/4HANA and BTP transformation, and enterprise cloud DevSecOps, serving enterprise customers primarily through its North American operations and global delivery organization.

business.body:
- **Geospatial:** Managed ArcGIS Cloud Services (MACS White Glove), Managed ArcGIS Cloud Services (MACS Advanced), GIS health checks, Utility network transformation services, GeoAI (AI-enabled spatial intelligence)

- **Enterprise Cloud:** Enterprise Cloud DevSecOps services

business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Continue an AI-first, Cloud-First strategy, sharpening delivery and products with an AI-first operating model.
- Remain deliberately niche across three focus areas — enterprise cloud, geospatial and SAP transformation — rather than pursue broad-based, volume-based IT services.
- Deepen hyperscaler alliances with Microsoft Azure and Amazon AWS as the core of the platform go-to-market strategy.
- Extend geospatial engineering depth into GeoAI (AI-enabled spatial intelligence) across utilities, government, public safety, healthcare, logistics and manufacturing.
- Grow the SAP practice across the full transformation lifecycle (S/4HANA migration, SAP HANA Cloud, BTP, Clean Core) using a growing AI-accelerated migration practice.
- Invest in high-demand capabilities including GenAI, SAP BTP and Azure ArcGIS Enterprise solutions through focused upskilling and strategic hiring.
- Maintain a debt-free balance sheet and ample cash reserves to absorb near-term demand pressures while continuing selective, long-term investment.
outlook.title: Strategy

outlook.body:
- Global macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainties are expected to continue affecting near-term client spending.
- Growth is led by the durability of the annuity-based managed services model, complemented by selective, high-value transformation engagements.
- The company chose to invest ahead of demand during the year, which had some near-term impact but was intentional, reflecting a shift toward AI-enabled offerings and NextGen talent.
- Cautious technology spending characterized the demand backdrop during the year.
- The North American business, anchored by U.S. operations and supported by the global engineering organization, remains a key pillar of the business.
